references.text: Describes what is to be done with the goat on which the lot falls for Azazel – it shall be presented alive before the Lord to make atonement and sent away into the wilderness.
The one who leads the goat out to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water before he returns to the camp.
Casting lots is used here to divide the land, the same method used to choose between the two goats.
Joshua casts lots for the Lord at Shiloh to divide the land, showing casting of lots as a holy method for determining God's will.
The lot is cast into the lap, but the decision comes from the Lord – confirming that casting lots was seen as a way to seek God's will.
The suffering servant bears everyone's sins, a prophetic parallel to the scapegoat who carries the people's sins out into the wilderness.
The book of Hebrews refers to the high priest entering the Most Holy Place once a year with blood for the people's sins, which is the context for casting lots between the two goats.
Christ entered the sanctuary with his own blood and won eternal redemption, fulfilling the atonement ritual represented by the two goats.
